story.originalTitle: 'He's so far below my level' - Verstappen taunts Russell over Las Vegas GP error
story.summaryEn: Max Verstappen said George Russell is "so far below my level" after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix, taunting the Mercedes driver over a major error in the race.
detailZh: 维斯塔潘在嘲讽对手在拉斯维加斯大奖赛中的重大失误后，称乔治·拉塞尔“远低于他的水平”。
红牛车手马克斯·维斯塔潘赢下拉斯维加斯大奖赛，并在梅赛德斯车手乔治·拉塞尔说出“我不会接受有人坑我”之后对其予以抨击；两人此前在最后一次练习赛中发生碰撞；拉塞尔在周日正赛中撞车，最终排名第九。

马克斯·维斯塔潘在赢下拉斯维加斯大奖赛后，对梅赛德斯车手作出尖锐回应，称乔治·拉塞尔“远低于我的水平”。
维斯塔潘凭借一场惊人的防守驾驶拿下本赛季第四场胜利，而拉塞尔在比赛后段撞车，最终获得第九名，此前他曾与维斯塔潘争夺冠军。
两人在周六的最后一节练习中相撞，维斯塔潘因该事件中“驾驶不稳定”而受到警告，但拉塞尔批评了这位红牛车手。

“规则里没有任何条款说不能超越一个正在开始飞驰圈的人，但当你这么做时，你就是在坑害这个人，而他每周都这样对待许多车手，大家都接受了，”他告诉天空意大利。
“我不会就这么接受有人这样坑害我，还像他们比所有人都更大更好一样四处走动。总得有人站出来对抗那家伙。”
乔治·拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯大奖赛试图超越队友基米·安东内利时锁死轮胎撞上护栏，这让对手马克斯·维斯塔潘大为高兴
维斯塔潘在第三次赢得拉斯维加斯大奖赛后的赛后新闻发布会上被问及这些言论，并回击了拉塞尔。
他说：“问题是，他在赛道外话很多。老实说，这对我来说并不真的困扰，因为他远低于我的水平，所以对我来说，试图去挑战这一点根本没有任何意义。所以，这并不困扰我。”
“而今天，因果报应真是个婊子。老实说，当我看向后视镜，看到正在发生的事情时，那真是太棒了[当拉塞尔撞车时]。我当时想，‘太棒了，我的一天只会越来越好。’
“当然，当我随后以第一名冲过终点线时，我的一天圆满了。”
马克斯·维斯塔潘在赢得拉斯维加斯大奖赛后，对老对手乔治·拉塞尔说了几句选择性的言辞。

detailEn: Max Verstappen says George Russell 'so far below his level' after poking fun at rival for major error during Las Vegas GP

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix and hit out at George Russell after the Mercedes driver said "I'm not going accept somebody to screw me over" after the pair collided in final practice; Russell crashed during Sunday's race and finished down in ninth
Highlights from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix
Max Verstappen says George Russell is "so far below my level" in a scathing response to the Mercedes driver after winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Verstappen claimed his fourth win of the season after a stunning defensive drive while Russell crashed in the latter stages and finished ninth, having battled Verstappen for the win earlier.
The pair collided in final practice on Saturday with Verstappen warned for "driving erratically" in the incident but Russell criticised the Red Bull driver.

"There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it," he told Sky Italy.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
George Russell hits the barrier after a lock-up when trying to overtake team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, much to the delight of rival Max Verstappen
Verstappen was asked about the comments in the post-race press conference following his third Las Vegas Grand Prix victory and hit back at Russell.

He said: "The thing is, he speaks a lot next to the track. And honestly, for me, it doesn't really bother me because he's so far below my level that it doesn't really make any sense for me anyway to try and challenge that. So, it doesn't bother me.
"And today, karma is a b****. It was honestly fantastic when I looked in my mirror and I saw what was happening [when Russell crashed]. I was like, 'fantastic, my day is only getting better.'
"And of course, when I then crossed the line in first, my day was complete."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
